subject: general
question: Two coils, A and B, have self-inductances of 120 μH and 300 μH, respectively. When a current of 1 A flows through coil A, it induces a flux linkage of 100 μWb turns in coil B. What is the mutual inductance between the coils?
solution: The correct answer is __100 μH****.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The formula for mutual inductance is: **M = N₂(Φ₂)/I₁**, where: • M__ is the mutual inductance. • __Φ₂__ is the flux linkage in the second coil due to current in the first coil. • __I₁__ is the current in the first coil. • Given Φ₂ = 100 μWb turns and I₁ = 1 A, the mutual inductance is: **M = 100 μWb / 1 A = 100 μH.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** • **Self-Inductance:** • It is the property of a coil by which it opposes any change in the current passing through it. • It depends on the number of turns, area of cross-section, and material used. • **Mutual Inductance:** • It is the property of two coils when the magnetic field of one induces an EMF in the other. • It depends on the relative positions and orientations of the coils. • **Inductance Units:** • The unit of inductance is Henry (H). • 1 H = 1 Weber turn per Ampere. 8d:Tde4,
